findings.description: The generated PM has reconcile.enabled false, so the canonical PM heartbeat performs checkpoint-only ticks instead of its required sentinel duties.
Ticket provisioning leaves .project.json noncanonical: reintroduces board_url, keeps state planned, and preserves identifier SSBN while binding the live SSBNK board.
Immediate post-deploy pj audit exits 1 because mise.config-root is not converged to the generated PM launcher path.
Dry-run and live summaries contradict reality: dry-run says Provisioned, live reports a GitHub runtime and usable Telegram ingress, and provisioning logs say voxxy while effective config is vox.
Provisioning reports the canonical subagent-driven-development PM skill missing but continues and declares the PM ready.
Local Copier rendering includes ignored __pycache__ and pyc runtime droppings from the vendored template worktree because source exclusions are incomplete.
The shipped command surface has untested broken/stale paths: --email requires a missing 50-email.sh and --force-config can regenerate a schema older than the pinned template.
Vendored fleet-sync reports 148 false drifts because it still expects config.yaml symlinks instead of real generated base-plus-delta profiles.

The shared Hermes runtime environment contains credential-shaped literal values in a file; host policy requires moving secrets to 1Password/runtime injection and retaining no plaintext credential file.
No direct full-live regression covers pj hermes-agent --yes, immediate audit health, deferred gateway behavior, or summary truthfulness.
Invalid finding text created by shell interpolation; corrected and superseded by F013.
Provisioning emits a non-portable cp -n warning and PTY-captured summary collapses to one character per line when terminal width is zero.
Official pj hermes-agent --yes exits zero and claims success while its newly enabled gateway restart loops with exit 78 because the same mode skips Telegram credentials.
The authoritative patch release script hard codes PJAN-44 in its release commit message, so a PJAN-86 release would violate the active ticket attribution contract.
Four tracked Hermes env backup files retain already-vault-planned plaintext credentials; repository policy requires deleting tracked backups and verifying no secret-bearing copy remains.
Additive Hermes host config bootstrap corrupts valid TOML when table headers have inline comments or array tables are present.
Parent commit and PJAN-86 test can pass against a mutable newer submodule worktree while the recorded Hermes template gitlink remains stale.
Noninteractive overwrite protection checks only role.yaml, so a nonempty partial Hermes role directory can be mutated before Copier conflicts.
Systemd migration can enable installed units without updating durable service_state from installed to active, leaving audit and migration red.
Hermes config bootstrap dry run returns success without printing its plan because the standalone CLI drops successful command messages.
The authoritative release transaction disables all repository hooks during the release commit, violating the global guard policy.
Ticket provider provisioning can replace malformed or nonobject project JSON with a minimal manifest and then bootstrap a duplicate external board instead of failing before mutation.
Credentialed gateway provisioning claims active after a single is-active sample with no stabilization window, allowing an immediate crash loop to be reported as success.
Channel credential verification passes raw tokens through extra child environments and command arguments despite the stdin-only minimal-environment contract.
Legacy Hermes profile symlinks are followed and role-owned state is deleted through the symlink before migration can reject or convert the profile.
Ticket provider provisioning does not lock the complete read check-create write sequence or atomically replace project JSON, so concurrent runs can create duplicate boards and lose a binding.
Vox reconciliation copies the entire fleet plugin list into the profile delta, freezing inherited plugins, re-enabling intentional exclusions, and preventing later base changes from propagating.
A transient 1Password validation outage downgrades valid Telegram or Slack wiring to deferred and removes its done marker even though the durable vault reference remains valid.
Registry reruns replace the complete agent row, discard extension metadata, and generate a new provisioned timestamp, so a successful second run is not byte-identical.
The immutable Hermes Skillex core omits 33god-projects in fallback behavior and can be reduced by configuration or environment overrides instead of only extended.

Generated profile deltas inherit Telegram enabled from the fleet base even when channel provisioning is deferred missing or invalid, so an ordinary restart can turn a previously latent mismatch into an exit 78 gateway failure.
Final Hermes help text still implies that normal deployment may create a per-agent GitHub runtime repository even though the canonical local ignored runtime architecture never creates one.
Systemd stabilization accepts an activating heartbeat and returns after three samples before its declared six-sample deadline, so a delayed exit or restart can still be persisted as healthy.
Slack provisioning validates only bot authentication and xapp token syntax, then enables Socket Mode without authenticating the required app-level token.
Vox fleet convergence uses substring matching so stale voxxy provider and plugin values can be mistaken for canonical vox values and left unrepaired.
Advancing the Hermes template gitlink leaves the tracked pjangler PM Plane provider stale against the canonical template, making the full PJAN-50 regression and aggregate suite fail.
Existing-role overwrite protection ignores placeholder names without rejecting symlink placeholders, so a symlink named gitkeep or operating-system metadata can bypass the force gate.
The release transaction does not revalidate the final commit subject after normal hooks, so a successful commit-msg hook can rewrite the PJAN-86 attribution and still pass all post-commit gates.

Two local-only detached runtime commits remain reachable through Git reflogs and retain plaintext credentials in object storage even though no remote ref or GitHub commit knows those objects; exact local purge or coordinated rotation is required.

A post-install Hermes TOML validator failure can invoke the same unavailable validator before restoration and leave the unverified candidate in place instead of first restoring the exact operator config.

Hermes template config recovery, snapshot, merge, and installation are not one serialized window, so two concurrent bootstraps can both accept the same stale operator snapshot and last-writer-wins overwrite.

Tokenless Slack and Telegram reruns snapshot durable references, verified identity, and allow-list policy before the registry and profile locks, allowing stale state to overwrite a completed concurrent rotation.
Initial profile config.delta.yaml seeding checks and writes outside the canonical profile lock, so it can truncate a populated delta created by a concurrent conforming writer.

A still-valid Plane credential and retired dashboard credential remain reachable in pushed history of four private runtime remotes even though current tips are clean; authorized rotation or retirement plus coordinated history rewrite is required.

Installed-config rollback and prepared crash recovery overwrite a newer canonical config written by a non-cooperating process instead of CAS-checking the transaction candidate and retaining recovery evidence.

A pre-existing hardlink alias lets another writer mutate the supposedly protected operator inode during validation, defeating exact byte and mtime rollback because original link topology is not rejected.

Channel, voice, renderer, absorb, and fleet backfill paths mutate the same profile delta and generated config through inconsistent lock domains, so valid concurrent changes can be lost despite each individual atomic write succeeding.

Locked multi-file channel transactions have no compare-and-swap guard against an out-of-band operator edit after snapshot, and their unconditional rollback can overwrite newer state; a real tokenless Slack rerun silently erased a concurrent config.delta.yaml edit while returning success.
First channel credentials entered through the interactive prompt bypass the pre-verification disable transaction, so failed remote validation can leave a never-verified profile inherited-enabled.
A tokenless Slack or Telegram rerun with only a new allow-list reports reconciliation but reloads the old runtime policy, making authorization-only changes silently ineffective.

The channel multi-file transaction has no durable crash journal; process death between disabled refs, runtime policy, role identity, registry claim, activation, and marker can leave mixed generations that a later tokenless run accepts.
Generic profile delta mutation modes still expose secret-reference and channel-enabled writes under only the profile lock, bypassing the required registry-before-profile transaction order.

Channel transaction code relies on an unenforced outer registry lock, while the shell lock uses check-then-follow redirection; direct invocation or a lock-path swap can mutate state without the intended lock domain or follow the wrong inode.
Fleet synchronization distributes the new profile seeder but not every changed channel lifecycle and transaction asset, so deployed roles can remain on stale unsafe code while appearing synchronized.
A never-configured tokenless channel requires the reference validator before its locked role snapshot is inspected, turning safe deferral into a hard failure when the validator is unavailable.
Production channel lock code contains environment-controlled test barriers that can pause execution or write caller-selected paths, and derived readiness paths are not proven symlink-safe.
Profile lock timeout parsing accepts positive infinity, violating the bounded-wait contract and allowing a blocked mutation to hang forever.
Tokenless allow-list parsing takes the first duplicate environment assignment although shell runtime semantics use the last, so reconciliation can activate the wrong effective policy.

Locked channel snapshots are not cross-checked against agent/profile binding arguments and managed YAML duplicates are updated only at the first occurrence, allowing stale or ineffective identity metadata writes.
Profile delta seeding uses unconditional replacement after an absence check, so an out-of-band operator file created in that interval is silently overwritten despite the profile lock.

Successful Hermes config validation checks a stale candidate snapshot, then commits and releases the protected original even if a newer canonical file replaced the candidate during validation; plain check-then-rename also lacks an atomic install CAS against out-of-band replacement.
